chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Bostic and West at college, Luther West's draft, and the Catholic teacher Freeman
summary: Bostic at Creighton, West at Xavier, West's induction and Love's 1943 call from Fields; Mr. Freeman taught both boys.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: By the way, did you know that Bostic went to school here in Omaha, at Creighton University?
Yes, he and another young man from there, Sam Abner.
One or the other. He's from Tulsa too. He came here and West, they weren't exactly the same classmates, very close, but West went to Xavier in New Orleans.
By the way, so Luther would play with you just intermittently and go back to school?

Yeah, he would go back to school, until, I think, he left one year and we got going pretty good and he wouldn't go back. Then he was inducted in the service and then came back again when he was out of the service. That was Spurgeon, when he was inducted in the service, when I tried to get you.
By the way, where did he get the name Spurgeon?
I don't know how that nickname came about.

You called me in 1943 and I was working--Johnny Littles and I were working at Sloppy Joe's, to join your band. You called me several times and I joined Basie--I was going to join you and Basie came and took me September 4, 1943.

Anyway, Bostic went on and they were all right and he came out just overnight, just saxophone fine, and then it was Freeman, a Catholic teacher--both of those boys were Catholics--and they went to the public school but they also studied Catholic and this Catholic teacher was music, and he got a little band. So they really had teaching two ways, from them, and then from the high school band too, and they kind of doubled up on things. They were very good, and Mr. Freeman was just wild about Spurgeon and Bostic.
